stem: A well 4-year-old has scattered petechiae after a viral illness. He is playful, has no fever, bone pain or hepatosplenomegaly. Platelets are 9 × 10⁹/L; haemoglobin and white-cell count are normal. There is no mucosal bleeding, and reliable follow-up is available. Which management is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Observation with safety advice and early review
options.explanation: Correct. Skin-only bleeding in a well child with isolated thrombocytopenia and reliable follow-up is managed by observation, bleeding precautions and paediatric review, regardless of the count alone.

options.label: B
options.text: Oral prednisolone because petechiae are present
options.explanation: Treatment is guided by clinical bleeding and context; petechiae alone do not mandate steroids.

options.label: C
options.text: Bone marrow aspirate before any treatment decision
options.explanation: Typical isolated thrombocytopenia without bone pain, organomegaly or other cytopenias does not need marrow examination.

options.label: D
options.text: IV immunoglobulin to lift the count quickly
options.explanation: IVIG is not routinely needed for skin-only bleeding in a well child with reliable follow-up.

options.label: E
options.text: Platelet transfusion because the count is below 10
options.explanation: Platelet transfusion is reserved for life-threatening bleeding; transfused platelets are rapidly destroyed in ITP.

context: In childhood immune thrombocytopenia, treatment decisions are driven by bleeding severity, examination and circumstances rather than the platelet count alone. Provide bleeding precautions, medication advice, follow-up and a clear return plan.
